This disease is called dieback."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Describe the significance of dietary fiber.","marks":0,"answer":"Fibrous food or roughage is found in the outer covering of cereals, vegetables, skin of fruits, stem of plants, roots, leaves, etc. These are the cellulose and lignin of cell walls. Roughage absorbs water, increases the amount of feces and helps to eliminate stools. Roughage-enriched food also absorbs harmful products from the intestine. It is assumed that roughage reduces the risk of cancer to some extent. Roughage plays a role in reducing obesity, the tendency of fat deposition, and hunger."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Calculate the daily calorie demand of Shafin.","marks":0,"answer":"According to the stem, Age of Shafin = 16 years, Height = 5 feet 1 inch ≈ 155 cm, Weight = 80 kg.
BMR of men = \( 66 + (13.7 \times \text{weight in kg}) + (5 \times \text{height in cm}) - (6.8 \times \text{age in years}) \)
So, BMR of Shafin = \( 66 + (13.7 \times 80) + (5 \times 155) - (6.8 \times 16) \)
\[
= 66 + 1096 + 775 - 108.8 = 1828.2 \text{ kcal}
\]
Since Shafin is light industrious, plays 2–3 days a week, his daily calorie demand = BMR × 1.375
\[
= 1828.2 \times 1.375 = 2513.775 \text{ kcal}
\]"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"How much weight should Shafin lose in relation to the average value of ideal BMI for good health? Analyze mathematically.","marks":0,"answer":"Shafin's BMI = \( \frac{80}{(1.55)^2} = 33.29 \)
Ideal BMI range = 18.5 – 24.9
For ideal BMI 24.9, weight = \( 24.9 \times (1.55)^2 \approx 59.83 \text{ kg} \)
Weight to lose = \( 80 - 59.83 \approx 20.17 \text{ kg} \)
So, Shafin should lose about 20 kg to reach ideal BMI.
---"}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is chlorosis?","marks":0,"answer":"Without chlorophyll, green leaves gradually turn yellow. The condition of leaves becoming yellow is called chlorosis."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is ATP compared to rechargeable battery?","marks":0,"answer":"Everything is completed by energy released from the breaking down of the chemical bond of ATP. The food we eat is oxidized and the energy released from this oxidation is used to create ATP through phosphorylation. It breaks down when energy is needed and combines taking energy from food. For this reason, ATP is compared to rechargeable battery."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the total energy from the given food of the stem.","marks":0,"answer":"According to the food calorie content, 4, 4 and 9 food calories are found from 1 gm of carbohydrates, proteins and lipids respectively.
Food calories from 300 gm of rice and bread = \( 300 \times 4 = 1200 \text{ kcal} \)
Food calories from 200 gm of meat and pulses = \( 200 \times 4 = 800 \text{ kcal} \)
Food calories from 50 gm of oil and butter = \( 50 \times 9 = 450 \text{ kcal} \)
Total = \( 1200 + 800 + 450 = 2450 \text{ kcal} \)
We know, 1 kcal = 4.2 kJ
So, \( 2450 \text{ kcal} = 2450 \times 4.2 = 10290 \text{ kJ} \)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"How foods of the stem become digested? Analyze it.","marks":0,"answer":"Rice and wheat are carbohydrates, meat and dal are proteins, and oil and butter are lipids. After ingestion, food is broken down into small particles by teeth and tongue in the oral cavity and mixed with saliva. Ptyalin in saliva converts carbohydrate into maltose. In stomach, pepsin converts proteins into polypeptides. In small intestine, amylase converts maltose into glucose, trypsin converts polypeptides into amino acids, and lipase converts lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.
---"}]
